units.text: Homage to him, the blessed one, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha! Some stand on a sure bet, while sophists speak of a second way. An intelligent person, knowing this, would take up the sure bet.
Digging untiringly in a sandy waste, there at the underground stream he found water. In the same way, a sage with strength aroused untiringly finds the peace of the heart.
If you fail to achieve certainty regarding the true teaching you’ll regret it for a long time, like this wanton merchant.
Even with a little capital the intelligent and clear-seeing man uplifts himself, like a tiny flame when fanned.
“Speak, O King: what value has a cup of rice for the pricing of horses?” “He values a cup of rice at Varanasi with its suburbs!”
Endowed with conscience and prudence, and comprised of bright qualities, the good and true persons in the world are said to have godly qualities.
I am your son, Great King! Provide for me, ruler of the people. The king provides for others, what then of his own offspring?
Even though they do not hurry, one who hopes for the fruit succeeds. I am one whose spiritual life has ripened: know this, chief.
Growing on top of my head, these thieves of life have sprouted. Messengers of the gods have appeared— it is time for me to go forth.
He who is not guarded by others, and who does not guard others, truly sleeps at ease, O King, unconcerned for sensual pleasures.
The virtuous ones prosper, who live extending protection. See Lucky Spot coming, surrounded by their family circle; then see this Black Mark, bereft of family.
Befriend only Banyan, stay away from Branch. Better is death with Banyan than life with Branch.
Curse the dart, the arrow that deeply strikes a man. Curse the nation where women rule. Those creatures are cursed who fall to women’s sway.
Nothing, it seems, is worse than tastes in monasteries or meeting places. The domesticated Wind-deer was brought under Victor’s sway by tastes.
“Please accept the eight-hooved ass, the deer more wily than the wily.” “He has skipped the appointment seven times— I’ll make no attempt to instruct him.”
“About that deer—triply collapsed with many illusions, eight-hooved, a midnight drinker— he’s breathing on the ground through one nostril! Excelling with these six tricks, he deserves a chance.”
Whether the moon is waning or waxing, it is cool when the gale blows. Since the wind brings the cool, both are undefeated in this instance.
If beings only knew how this suffering is created by birth, no creature would kill another, for the slayer of creatures grieves.
If you would be released, after death might you be released, because releasing binds. That’s not how the attentive are released; such release is the fool’s bondage.
Seeing footprints go down into the water, and none that return, we shall drink water through a reed: no way shall you kill me.
The four-horned antelope knows that it’s you who tosses fruit from the beechwood tree. I’ll go to another beechwood, I don’t like your fruit.
The dogs raised in the royal family, pedigreed, handsome and strong, are not slaughtered, we are slaughtered— this is not the mutts deserving death, <j>this is the killing of the weak.
Though lying on my side pierced by many arrows, the king’s stallion beats a gelding— harness me now, charioteer.
Whenever whenever, wherever whenever, wherever wherever, whenever whenever: the thoroughbred drives onward, while the geldings fade right there.
At one ford or another lead the horse to drink, rider. For man who overeats, even milk-rice is a torment.
Before, hearing the speech of the bandits, Ladyface went on a rampage. But hearing the speech of the well-restrained, the supreme elephant is established <j>in all good qualities.
It’s not enough to give him a morsel, a bite, some grass, or a rubbing-down. I think by seeing the dog often, the elephant grew fond of him.
One should only speak sweetly, never not sweetly. For the one speaking sweetly, a large load was pulled, earning him money, and he was satisfied with that.
No matter how heavy the load, or how deep the passage, when they harness Black, he pulls that load.
Envy not what is Munika’s, for he eats the food of the terminally ill. Don’t worry, just eat your chaff, this is a mark of long life.
Mātali, don’t ram the bird nests in the red silk-cotton woods with your draft-pole. I’d rather give up our lives to the titans than deprive these birds of their nests.
Your cry is sweet, your back brilliant, your neck the color of sapphire, and your feathers a full fathom long; still, because of your dancing, I will not give you my daughter.
In agreement, the birds fly, taking away the net. But when they start arguing they’ll come under my sway.
It’s not the cold or heat for me, nor the being caught in the net; it’s that my lady, the fish, thinks of me, “He went for joy to another.”
I have wings that do not fly! I have feet that do not walk! Mother and father have fled! Jātaveda the fire: go back!
You sky-flyers staying near the great evergreen, this fire is emerging! Geese! Flee to the quarters! The threat is born from the refuge!
Those people who honor the elder are experts in the teaching; praised in this life, they’re destined for happiness in lives to come.
The clever cheat cannot achieve ultimate happiness by cheating. The clever cheat succeeds only in getting what the crane did from the crab.
I suspect the heap of gold and golden chains is where the house-born slave Nandaka stands yelling curses.
Fine, let me fall head over heels into hell, but I shall not do what is ignoble. Please accept my alms offering.
One who does not follow advice when instructed by an ally who desires their good, grieves like Mittaka hanging off a goat’s foot.
One who does not follow advice when instructed by an ally who wants to help, not following the pigeon’s counsel, ends up in the hands of their foes.
One who does not follow advice when instructed by an ally who wants to help, ends up destroyed like the pole acrobat’s father.
Better is a considerate foe than an inconsiderate friend. Thinking, “I shall kill the mosquito”, the idiot son split open his father’s head.
Better is an intelligent foe than a foolish sympathizer. See that wretched Rohinī, grieving after killing her mother.
Surely not with one who misunderstands the meaning does good conduct lead to happiness. The simpleton destroys the good, like the monkey groundskeeper.
Surely not with one who misunderstands the meaning does good conduct lead to happiness. The simpleton destroys the good, as Koṇḍañña did the toddy.
Who wishes to profit by inappropriate means is tormented. The Cetans who killed Vedabbha all fell into ruin.
Waiting for a constellation, a fool lets the good pass them by. The good is the constellation of the good; for what do the stars matter?
A sacrifice of simpletons by the thousand was pledged by me. Now I shall sacrifice many an unrighteous man.
A man should have hope, the astute should not be disillusioned. Now I truly see myself— as I wished, so I became.
A man should make an effort the astute should not be disillusioned. Now I truly see myself, lifted from the water to the shore.
The cups stay just as full, while the ignorant talk goes on. For this reason I know this is not an excellent beer.
This tree is not hard to climb, nor is it far from the village. For this reason I know this tree is not sweet-fruited.
He whose heart is not stuck, a man of intrepid mind, develops skillful qualities for the sake of sanctuary from the yoke. Gradually he would attain the ending of all fetters.
He whose heart is well-forged, a man of cheerful mind, develops skillful qualities for the sake of sanctuary from the yoke. Gradually he would attain the ending of all fetters.
Whoever possesses these four qualities like you, lord of langurs— truth, principle, steadfastness, and generosity— escapes the visible foe.
Whoever possesses these three qualities like you, lord of langurs— adroitness, heroism, wisdom— escapes the visible foe.
Blow, blow, don’t overblow, for overblowing is bad. By blowing a hundred was gained, by overblowing it was lost.
Blow, blow, don’t overblow, for overblowing is bad. By blowing riches were earned, but your blowing dad blew it.
The women in the world called unclaimed— there is no confining them. They are rude and full of desires, like an all-consuming flame. Leaving them behind, I shall go forth and foster seclusion.
The brahmin who played the harp while blindfolded had raised his wife since infancy— who would ever trust such women?
Hateful ingrates! Slanderous traitors! Live the spiritual life, mendicant, you will not be bereft of happiness.
Do not rejoice, “She loves me,” nor lament, “She loves me not.” The mood of women is hard to understand, like the track of fish in water.
Just like rivers and roads, taverns, hotels, and pubs, are those called women in the world. Sages do not get angry with them.
One wish I had in the past, before I won Queen Sweetheart. But when I won the moon-eyed lady, wish upon wish was born.
A son in my lap, Your Majesty, or a husband while walking the street— but I don’t see the place from where I can fetch a brother.
In whom the mind settles, and the heart too is confident— gladly one would trust in that man not seen before.
Curse that vomited poison, which I vomited for the sake of life and now shall consume again. Death is better for me than life!
That victory is not a good victory which may be undone. That victory is a good victory which may not be undone.
Whoever wishes to do afterwards tasks they should have done before, like the one who broke a branch off the Warding Tree, afterwards is tormented by regrets.
An ungrateful person, always looking for opportunity, even if given the whole earth, would still not be satisfied.
The truth, it seems, was spoken by certain people here— better a floating log than a certain person.
It is well for the many relatives, the trees born in the forest. The wind sweeps off one standing alone, even the enormous lord of the forest.
Thunder forth, Pajjuna! Disperse the trove of the crow! Subject the crow to sorrow, and free me from sorrow!
I am unsuspecting in the village; in the wilderness there’s no peril for me: I ride upon the straight path with love and compassion.

“Bulls; trees; cows; oxen; horse; bronze goblet; she-jackal; water-pot; lotus pond; uncookable rice; sandalwood; pumpkins sink; stones float; frogs swallow black cobras; golden swans surround a crow; the wolf trembles for fear of the sheep.” No perversion of reality is happening here for me.
Both are lame, both crippled, both cross-eyed, and both covered in warts: I see not which is Herring.
When cows were plundered and killed, houses burned down, and people abducted, then came the son of she whose son is dead, sounding the harsh drum of war.
That is good for some, ill for others. Therefore not all is good, nor is all ill.

This Clear-eyed One arises, the One King, palomino-colored, shining over the earth. I bow especially to you, palomino-colored, shining over the earth: guarded by you let us live out this day. Those brahmins who are knowledge-masters with respect to all things, I worship them, may they keep me safe. Hail the Awakened Ones, hail Awakening! Homage to the freed ones, homage to freedom! Having made this protection, the peacock wanders seeking. This Clear-eyed One sets, the One King, palomino-colored, shining over the earth. I bow especially to you, palomino-colored, shining over the earth: guarded by you let us live out this night. Those brahmins who are knowledge-masters with respect to all things, I worship them, may they keep me safe. Hail the Awakened Ones, hail Awakening! Homage to the freed ones, homage to freedom! Having made this protection, the peacock made his home.

“Those folk sow and reap, men living on the fruit of their work. They have no share of this island. This is better far than India!” “When the fifteenth day full moon has risen, there will be a great flood from the sea, drowning this splendid isle. Let it not destroy you all! Go to some other haven!” “Never shall a mighty flood of water from the sea drown this splendid isle— I have seen that through many a sign. Don’t fear! Why worry? Celebrate! You’ve come to this splendid abode, full of food and drink. I see no danger for you at all. Celebrate, even unto the sons of sons!” “This god in the southern quarter crying, ‘It is safe!’: his is the truth! The northern doesn’t know if there’s a danger or not. Don’t fear! Why worry? Celebrate!” “As these spirits argue, one reporting danger, one safety, please heed my advice, lest we perish swift and fleet. Let all join together to build a boat, a strong vessel fully equipped. If this southern one speaks true, and is falsely rejected by the northern, it shall serve us in time of need, and we would not give up the island. But if the northern speaks true, and is falsely rejected by the southern, then having all boarded the boat, we shall cross safely to the far shore. Truly, best not accept the last word that came your way, when what was spoken by the first was best. Who here accepts the truth after examination, that man goes to the best place.” Just as, in the middle of the watery sea, the merchants fled to safety by their own efforts, so, realizing his future welfare, he of vast wisdom transgresses not at all. Fools deluded by desire for tastes, not realizing their future welfare, sink down in face of present need, like those people in mid-ocean. Prepare what must be done for the future, thinking, “Let what must be done not harm me on the day the duty ripens.” The kind who acts to prepare what must be done, is not harmed by what must be done on the day the duty ripens.
Bhāsvaravarṇa occurs at Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 6.2.14. There it describes a man’s soul purified by the fires of cremation. By this point in the Pali its use is more mundane.
